successors.name: Chatti
successors.text: 'around the middle of the Weser River', with the Angrivarii to the north and the Chatti to the southwest (a radius round Hameln and Minden, which the gazetteer lacks)

ledger.x: 58-52 BC: the Cherusci are first attested in Caesar's Gallic War, which says the Bacenis Forest protected the Suebi from them.
8 BC: the Cherusci are a dependent people of Rome.
9: Arminius's coalition destroys three legions and the dependence ends.
around 88: the Chatti defeat Chariomerus and the Cherusci fade from the record.

wars.name: Drusus's campaigns in Germania
wars.outcome: Drusus reached the Weser in 11 BC but turned back; in 9 BC he defeated an alliance of Sicambri, Cherusci and Suebi and died at the end of the campaign; in 8 BC the Cherusci's submission left them a dependent, friendly people.

wars.name: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest and Germanicus's campaigns
wars.outcome: In 9 AD Arminius's coalition destroyed three Roman legions under Varus; in 14-16 Germanicus ran reprisals with mixed success (Idistaviso, the Angrivarian Wall) and was recalled; the Cherusci were not destroyed.

wars.name: War between Arminius and Maroboduus
wars.outcome: A Cheruscan faction under Inguiomerus defected to Maroboduus in 17 AD (Cherusci page); the marcomanni dossier has the war of the two coalitions in 17 and Maroboduus's fall in 19.

certainty.note: Only river and forest names; no frontier.
